judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare consideration/reliance preamble; no operative term whose meaning could be contested beyond OCR garbling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reference to 'the statements in the declarations' is consistent with the Declarations page and Condition 1 (Premium); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core grant turns on 'ultimate net loss', 'retained limit' and 'to which this policy applies', each of which pushes the reader into other defined terms; scope questions about what the umbrella actually indemnifies are the classic battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Retained Limit definition (c034), the Professional Services Exclusion (c082-c083) and the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084), which adds a 'professional liability hazard' the exclusion appears to remove.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger 'not covered by any underlying coverage ... or any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured' is a conditional defense obligation whose reach can be argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against II(a)/(b) (c008, c009) on defense where underlying insurance does apply and against Condition 13 (c056), which deems underlying insurance to remain in force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'even if such suit is groundless, false or fraudulent' plus 'as it deems expedient' gives the insurer discretion whose limits could be construed, but the language is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the Asbestos Endorsement's express negation of any defense duty (c081) and with c008, defense obligations are allocated but not obviously contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete list of bond premiums with an express disclaimer of any obligation to furnish bonds; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Limit of Liability (c013/c084) and with c010 making such payments additional to ultimate net loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Post-judgment interest and taxed costs language is standard and self-limiting by reference to the applicable limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the Ultimate Net Loss definition (c033), which excludes legal expenses and interest, so the two dovetail rather than clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable expenses, other than loss of earnings, incurred at the company's request' is narrow and bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision addresses insured's cooperation expenses except Condition 3 (c046), which imposes duties without a payment term; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'covered by underlying insurance' is a short phrase carrying real weight — whether costs are 'covered' when the underlying insurer disputes coverage is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with c003 (defense only where no underlying coverage) and c009 (drop-down on exhaustion); the boundary between them is where a dispute would sit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'exhausted by an occurrence' and 'immediately in excess ... without intervening insurance' are conditions whose satisfaction is often argued, though the words are reasonably precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Loss Payable (c048), which requires the underlying limit actually to have been paid, and with c056's notice-of-exhaustion requirement; drop-down disputes turn on that combination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'except settlement of claims or suits' is compressed and could be read to swallow the additional-payments rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the Limit of Liability (c013/c084) and Ultimate Net Loss (c033) it is coherent, but which payments erode the limit is a live question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short saving clause for jurisdictions barring defense; the text is garbled but the mechanism is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses jurisdictional prohibition; no competing provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursement of amounts 'within the self insured retention stated in Item 4' is definite in wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the company pays within the SIR, while Insuring Agreement I and the Retained Limit definition (c034) make coverage attach only in excess of the retained limit — a genuine fit question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The aggregate proviso limited to 'products or completed operations hazards' leaves per-occurrence versus aggregate treatment of other losses arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly rewritten by the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084) and the declared limits are further amended by Endorsement No. 4 (c109) to $20,000,000, so three texts state the limit differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'occurrences happening anywhere' is about as definite as a territory clause gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two Policy Territory Amended endorsements (c105, c113) purport to amend territory provisions of a Hospital Professional Liability coverage part that is not part of this umbrella policy, creating a fit problem with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or similar law' is a catch-all after enumerated compensation statutes, but it is a long-settled formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the Employers Liability underlying policy in Item 7, which shows the parties expected employer liability cover above workers' compensation; some tension but standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate nuclear energy exclusion with named associations and statutory references; precise and inapplicable to a hospital's ordinary risks.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The paired definitions clause (c018) supplies the terms; no other provision competes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard nuclear material exclusion; the OCR is poor but the drafting is a familiar industry form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c016 and c018; nothing elsewhere grants nuclear cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely definitional, tied to the Atomic Energy Act; no operative reach of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Serves only exclusions (b) and (c) and matches them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause as captured is a fragment ('to loss of use of tangible property which has not been physically injured ... resulting from') running straight into the Definitions heading, so its operative content is incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Property Damage definition (c036), which affirmatively covers loss of use of undamaged property, so exclusion and definition pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any subsidiary ... and any other organization coming under the named insured's control of which it assumes active management' is genuinely vague — 'control' and 'active management' have no boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Additional Named Insureds endorsement (c085), which lists entities and denies automatic coverage for newly acquired ones, and against later endorsements adding campuses (c117, c120).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The captured text is badly fragmented, but the underlying formula (executive officers, directors, stockholders acting within the scope of duties) is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the D&O Exclusion (c076-c078), which removes directors and officers for 'wrongful acts' while insured status is granted here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Omnibus automobile insured wording, truncated in the copy but standard in form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Automobile Liability underlying policy in Item 7 and the intrafamily carve-out (c061).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'except insofar as coverage is provided in the underlying insurance as scheduled herein' is a following-form carve-out whose scope depends on an unquoted other policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The schedule in Item 7 lists no aircraft cover, so the carve-out may be empty; it also parallels the Aircraft definition (c039).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The care-custody-control limb 'to the extent the insured is under contract to provide insurance' is an odd qualifier that could be read several ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Care, Custody & Control Endorsement (c075) states a broader, unqualified version of the same exclusion, so the two overlap inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard sistership/recall exclusion; garbled but conventional and remote from a hospital's exposures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with the products hazard definition (c041); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of advertising offenses with the carve-back 'shall not relate to use of slogans' is confusingly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the Advertising Liability definition (c037), which affirmatively covers infringement of title or slogan, leaving the slogan treatment inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Racing and demolition-contest exclusion is specific and easily applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision grants such cover; nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sudden and accidental' is the single most litigated phrase in pollution coverage, and the enumerated substances plus 'other irritants' raises ejusdem generis questions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion endorsement (c093-c096) purports to replace this exclusion, so which text governs and whether the described exclusion matches this one is a real question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The captured text is a scrambled composite of watercraft/aircraft and contractual-insured provisions, so its operative meaning cannot be read off the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on the same territory as the Contractual Exclusion Endorsement (c057) and the aircraft exclusion (c023).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dangling fragment ('operations by or on behalf of the named insured or to facilities of or used by the named insured') with no subject.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It continues c029 and adds nothing that conflicts with other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'subject to all the limitations upon coverage under such policy other than the limits of the underlying insurer's liability' is a following-form rule whose reach depends on unquoted policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands insured status well beyond the Additional Named Insureds list (c085) and the Cross Suits Endorsement's 'Named Insured' vocabulary (c059), creating a fit question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Partnership/joint venture wording is conventional and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations mark the Named Insured as a corporation, so this limb is largely inoperative rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sum actually paid or payable in cash' combined with the exclusion of all loss and legal expenses is a definition insurers and insureds routinely read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with c010 (amounts additional to ultimate net loss), the Appeals condition (c047) and the Overlap Endorsement (c106), which promises indemnity for legal expenses the definition excludes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the greater of' the scheduled underlying limits plus other collectible insurance, or the SIR when underlying insurance is inapplicable, is a notoriously contested formula for when the umbrella attaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the SIR reimbursement clause (c012), Loss Payable (c048), Other Insurance (c052) and Maintenance of Underlying Insurance (c056), which pull in different directions on attachment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'shock, mental anguish' and a qualified discrimination limb ('except where prohibited by law ... not committed by or on behalf of the insured') that is difficult to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Personal Injury Endorsement (c058) strips out mental injury, anguish and shock, and the Discrimination Exclusion (c079) removes discrimination entirely, so the base definition contradicts two endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard two-limb property damage definition tied to the policy period; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the loss-of-use exclusion fragment (c019), but endorsement structure otherwise leaves it intact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'idea misappropriation under an implied contract' and 'unfair competition' are broad terms, though this is an industry-standard list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against the advertising-offense exclusion (c026) on slogans and titles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'accident ... including continuous or repeated exposure', 'neither expected nor intended from the standpoint of the insured', and the deeming rule for exposure to 'substantially the same general conditions' are the classic sources of number-of-occurrences and intent disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deeming rule interacts directly with the per-occurrence and aggregate limits (c013, c084) and the SIR-per-occurrence in Item 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition of aircraft; nothing contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only by the aircraft exclusion (c023); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a land motor vehicle, trailer or semi-trailer' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the omnibus auto insured clause (c022) and Item 7's auto policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition opens with 'personal injury and property damage' but conditions on 'the bodily injury or property damage', a mismatch of defined terms that changes what is captured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The aggregate limit in c013/c084 keys off the products hazard, so the mismatch has real consequences for the limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional completed operations definition; 'reliance upon a representation or warranty' is broad but familiar.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with c043's completion timings and with the aggregate proviso in c013/c084.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mechanical completion tests, with an express deeming provision; little room for argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c042; no conflict elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence pointing to the declarations; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Pay Plan Endorsement (c097-c098) supplies instalments, which supplements rather than contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive inspection with an express disclaimer of any safety undertaking; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision on inspection or audit was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'whenever it appears that an occurrence is likely to involve indemnity' and 'as soon as practicable' are open-textured triggers that generate late-notice litigation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c073) limits the effect of a failure of condition to cases where it increases the risk or contributes to the loss, materially cutting across this notice duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The appeal-cost mechanics are specific and capped; garbled text but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly adds costs above the limit, which fits c010 and the Ultimate Net Loss definition (c033).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall not attach until the amount of the underlying limit has been paid by or on behalf of the insured' is the phrase that fuels exhaustion/below-limits-settlement disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against the drop-down clause (c009) and the Maintenance of Underlying Insurance condition (c056), which deems underlying insurance in force regardless of actual payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The captured text is a garbled remnant of a no-action clause and cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c070) expressly deletes the 'Action Against Company' condition in its entirety and replaces it, so this text is superseded and inconsistent with the replacement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line bankruptcy clause, badly OCR'd but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same rule reappears in the Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c070), producing duplication rather than contradiction.
